assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural empirical models of demand and competition transformed analysis of differentiated-product markets and applied industrial organization.
assessment.attribution: Pakes, Berry, and Bresnahan are central architects, though the listed contribution has a wider set of essential contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively used for decades in research, merger analysis, and policy evaluation.
uncertainties: The breadth of the foundational contributor set makes a three-person allocation necessarily incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a highly influential explanation of trade patterns, aggregate productivity, and gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the pivotal contributor, with Helpman and Redding major developers of the broader research program.
assessment.maturity: Its predictions and methods have shaped trade theory and empirical work for more than two decades.
uncertainties: The precise boundary between this contribution and earlier new-trade-theory work remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The economic analysis of information goods, network effects, compatibility, and digital-market conduct became foundational for modern industrial organization.
assessment.attribution: Shapiro, Varian, and Farrell made distinct, central theoretical and policy-facing contributions; other listed scholars also have substantial claims.
assessment.maturity: The work has enduring influence and exceptional contemporary relevance in competition policy.
uncertainties: Digital-market economics is a broad field, complicating definition of a single prize-worthy discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative Ricardian models made welfare gains from trade and counterfactual trade-policy analysis operational with disciplined theory.
assessment.attribution: Costinot, Kortum, and Rodriguez-Clare are closely identified with core advances in this unified quantitative program.
assessment.maturity: The approach is well established and widely applied in contemporary trade research and policy analysis.
uncertainties: The literature relies on strong modeling and trade-cost assumptions whose empirical adequacy varies by application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of management practices established organizational quality as a consequential, measurable source of productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are central originators, with Sadun an important contributor to the organizational-capital research program.
assessment.maturity: Results have been replicated across countries and have influenced both research and management-policy debates.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation of measured management practices remains difficult in observational settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on tasks, trade shocks, and labor-market adjustment substantially changed understanding of wage inequality and regional economic disruption.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson have closely linked and identifiable contributions; Katz is also important to the broader agenda.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a large follow-on literature and materially influenced policy discussions.
uncertainties: The relative contributions of technology, trade, and institutional change are difficult to isolate fully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods provided influential tools for addressing unobserved heterogeneity and endogeneity in panel data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell, and Bond are directly associated with the principal methods in the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding standards in applied microeconometrics and have been extensively scrutinized.
uncertainties: Finite-sample and weak-instrument problems can make routine applications unreliable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of ambiguity gave decision theory rigorous alternatives to subjective expected utility and influenced economic analysis under deep uncertainty.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa and Epstein are foundational figures, with Marinacci a major contributor to the modern literature.
assessment.maturity: The theories are mature and widely used across decision theory, finance, and macroeconomics.
uncertainties: Empirical discrimination among competing ambiguity models remains limited.
